Source: http://www.desnews.com

Posted June 27, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: On this day in 1844, Joseph Smith, the founder of the Mormon Church, was brutally murdered by a mob in Illinois.

One of the saddest characteristics of human nature is that those who have been the targets of bigotry and persecution often do not learn the importance of tolerance, but instead think that they should be the ones doing the persecuting

156 years after the murder of Joseph Smith, the Mormon Church is rich and powerful enough to have its own newspaper, The Deseret News, which now advocates state violence against even sick and dying medical marijuana users. It is especially shameful that a Church owned paper would violate the 9th Commandment.

See
Marijuana Prohibition, Media Criticism, Copyrights and the 8th and 9th Commandments.

The editorial below demonstrates how well ignorance and arrogance go together.)

June 23, 2000
From The Deseret News
letters@desnews.com
http://www.desnews.com/

LEGALIZE POT? HOW ABSURD

If New Mexico Gov. Gary Johnson can be credited with anything worthwhile, it is that he has brought the idea of legalizing marijuana out into the open where sound reasoning and facts can expose it for the idiocy it is. No one should be taken in by his illogical reasoning, no matter how convincing it sounds.
See
NORML Director David Boaz Praises New Mexico Governor -- 2 Articles

Johnson took center stage last week at the Western Governors Association meeting in Honolulu and, as he does virtually everywhere he speaks, immediately launched into the " legalize pot " presentation with a missionary zeal. " Is it so far-fetched to think that if we legalize marijuana, use will go down? " he asked. The answer, of course, is yes. It's not only far-fetched, it's silly.
See
Legalize Marijuana and Reduce Use?
New Survey Puts Estimate of Dutch Marijuana Use Even More Below DEAland

" Should laws exist that protect us from ourselves? " he asked next. That's an interesting way to phrase the issue. Here is a better one: Should laws exist to protect people from substances that can cause serious harm to their bodies and lead them to do crazy, possibly dangerous, things? Once a state gives official sanction to the use of marijuana, ignorant people may easily be led to believe it is an innocent, harmless diversion. It is not.
See
Is marijuana really harmless, like everyone has been saying?
(MarijuanaNews note: Yes, " ignorant people may easily be led " to believe foolish things. That is the one thing that this editorial proves.)

Surprisingly, the governor did not invoke the Dutch example. He was smart to leave it alone. Drug-legalization proponents often refer to Holland's quarter-century experiment with legalized drugs as an example of how wonderful society could become. They do so based solely on conventional wisdom borne by users with clouded minds.
(MarijuanaNews note: Only marijuana users " with clouded minds " favor the Dutch approach? What a cheap ad hominem. They should be ashamed of themselves.)
See
Professor Of Medicine At The University Of Toronto Urges Canada To " Go Dutch " At Vancouver Conference On Health, Addictions And Social Justice.
and
 " The failure of Dutch drug policy " An Examination of Prohibitionist Propaganda and the Official Dutch Government Response -- Special To MarijuanaNews
and
Drug Czar’s Office Issues New " Fact Sheet " On " The Drug Situation in the Netherlands "

The facts spell complete and unqualified disaster.

Writing in the publication " Foreign Affairs " last year, author Larry Collins presented a frank and well-documented look at the Dutch experiment.
(MarijuanaNews note: This particularly pernicious piece has been very useful to the prohibitionists. The Drug Czar even used it to lie to the Congress.)
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan
and
Foreign Affairs Pushes The Party Line At the Highest Levels:
Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda for the Elites.
April's Reefer Madness Award Winner
and links

He found a nation that has become the drug trafficking center of Europe,
See
The DEA Is Telling UK Narks That " Britain's drug barons are exporting home grown, high grade cannabis to Holland in exchange for Dutch ecstasy. "
where drug use, particularly of marijuana, has increased and where dealers have developed a new, potent form of the drug called " Nederwiet " that didn't exist before legalization.
(MarijuanaNews note: Nederwiet is simply Dutch-grown marijuana, not " a new form " of marijuana. This is one of the many " errors " in Collins’ work. It is clear that the Deseret editors also know nothing about marijuana, Dutch or otherwise. The average potency of Dutch marijuana is around 9%THC -- about 2½ times the DEAland average of 3.5% to 4% THC, and roughly 1 ½ times the Canadian average of 6% THC, but comparable to the best grown in Canada and DEAland. In short, most of it is grown indoors.)
See
The Prohibitionists In Stockholm Reveal The Shocking Truth
About The Potency Of Dutch Marijuana
and
RCMP Annual Report On the " Drug Situation in Canada " Contradicts Staples Of the Prohibitionist Party Line. Exclusive To MarijuanaNews.
and links

He quotes the director of a Dutch drug-abuse rehabilitation center as saying, " We see more and more people getting into trouble with cannabis. "
(MarijuanaNews note: This is supposed to represent the view of the Jellinek Institute, but consider the following statement by Roel Verssemauers, deputy manager of prevention of Jellinek, " In general, we consider our policy [decriminalization] a success, though that doesn't mean there are no problems. " )
See
The Dutch Demonstrate Common Sense, and the Canadians – Even the Police – Seem Ready to Learn – 3 Articles

A London doctor describes heavy Nederwiet users suffering withdrawal symptoms similar to those produced by hard drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is truly nonsense. From the Drug Czar’s IOM report:
" A distinctive marijuana withdrawal syndrome has been identified, but it is mild and short-lived. " )
See
Is Marijuana Addictive? Analysis By Richard Cowan

Between 1984 and 1996, marijuana use among people ages 18 to 25 in Holland increased by well over 200 percent, Collins writes. Perhaps New Mexico's governor would like to explain again in detail why he thinks the opposite would happen here.
(MarijuanaNews note: Taking one set of numbers out of context is either dishonest or completely incompetent. There is some question about the 1984 numbers, but the fact is that Dutch adolescent marijuana use has always been below DEAland rates, even at their lowest in 1991. Moreover, marijuana use doubled in DEAland between 1992 and 1997 during the highest level of marijuana arrests in history.

15.6 percent of the Dutch have used marijuana, " a figure that places national lifetime use at the same level or lower as that found in France (16.0% in 1995), Germany (13.9% in 1995), or the UK (22.0% in 1996) and far lower than that of the US (32.9% in 1997.) " -- (source: European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction 1998; National Household Survey 1997 Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration 1997).
See
Final Report Of Dutch National Drug Use Survey Will Require New Lies From The Drug Czar:
Their Lifetime Cannabis Use Half of DEAland’s; Two-Thirds That of UK

Johnson and other legalization hucksters are quick to draw similarities between marijuana and alcohol. Indeed, both are harmful drugs. There is a difference, however, in how society perceives them. Unfortunately, moderate alcohol consumption is culturally acceptable in much of the United States. However, that is hardly a reason to urge that the culture accept another harmful drug, as well.
See
Great London Times Column and News From New Zealand Compare Marijuana and Alcohol
(MarijuanaNews note: In 1933, Utah cast the decisive vote repealing alcohol prohibition even though the Mormon Church opposes alcohol use.)

Predictably, the one governor who applauded Johnson was Hawaii's Gov. Ben Cayetano, who recently signed a law that legalizes marijuana for medical use in that state -- one of the more absurd examples of legislative quackery to hit the modern age.
See
Organized Quacks In Hawaii Continue To Support Arresting The Sick and Dying

Serious researchers believe marijuana contains certain compounds of medicinal value. But absolutely none of them recommends smoking the weed as a means of obtaining any benefit.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Absolutely none "? Again, arrogance and ignorance.)
See
Chairman of the House of Lords Science and Technology Committee
Criticizes UK Government’s Rejection Of Report On Medical Marijuana
– 2 Articles With 2 of the Worst Prohibitionist Arguments
and
Leading British Journals, The New Scientist And The Lancet, Cite The IOM Report -- 2 Articles
and
Finnish Medical Association Supports Medical Marijuana
And Says Its Negative Effects Have Been Greatly Exaggerated.

States can use drug courts and an emphasis on education and rehabilitation to help fight substance abuse problems. These have shown reasonable success. But legalization is nothing more than an admission of defeat.
(MarijuanaNews note: The other Salt Lake paper has shown better judgement, and addressed that last point)
See
Salt Lake Paper Defects From Drug War:
" The United States never has been engaged in a real war with such disastrous losses.
No foreign power has ever been able to divorce American citizens from or limit the individual liberties
this nation’s founders said were inalienable. " – Can Orrin Hatch Read?
